ff_lettuce_romaine.note: A single whole romaine head on a plain grey background; raw, clean, no text. (Rejected a CC0 grocery-shelf shot because of readable price tags.)

ff_cabbage_raw.note: Tight close-up of the cut face of a raw white cabbage head showing the layered leaves; unmistakably raw. Borderline only on framing (close crop rather than a whole head) - the alternative whole-head photo had a price sticker and brand packaging.

ff_carrot_raw.author: Evan-Amos

alt.en: A bunch of fresh carrots with green tops

ff_carrot_raw.note: Bundle of whole raw carrots with leafy tops on a white background (Evan-Amos, public domain); raw state is obvious.

ff_carrot_boiled.reason: 4 searches (boiled / cooked / steamed carrots, plain side dish) found only mixed plates, soups, salads or roasted carrots; nothing showing plain boiled carrots alone.

ff_onion_raw.author: Colin

alt.en: A whole brown onion

ff_onion_raw.note: One whole raw yellow/brown onion with papery skin on a white background; matches raw onion.

ff_onion_sauteed.author: ccbarr

alt.en: Sliced onions softened in a frying pan

ff_onion_sauteed.note: Sliced onions sauteed until soft and lightly golden in a stainless pan - the pan-sauteed state the catalog describes, not crispy deep-fried onion (crispy/fried-onion photos were rejected for that reason).

ff_garlic_raw.author: Ivar Leidus

alt.en: Garlic bulbs with a peeled clove

ff_garlic_raw.note: Whole raw garlic bulb, a split bulb and two cloves (one peeled) on a neutral studio background; raw garlic, clean and well lit.

ff_potato_boiled.author: IgorCalzone1

alt.en: Potatoes boiled in their skins

ff_potato_boiled.note: Close-up of three 'Pellkartoffeln' (potatoes boiled in their skins), skins moist and split from cooking, on kitchen paper. Matches boiled-in-skin. Borderline: an in-skin boiled potato looks similar to a washed raw one; the cracked, glossy skin is the cooked cue. (A second candidate of peeled potatoes in a cluttered backlit kitchen was not used.)

ff_potato_baked.reason: Every baked/jacket potato found on Commons is topped (cheese, beans, chili, butter, chicken mayo) or part of a restaurant plate; no plain baked potato with skin.

ff_french_fries_oven.author: Keith McDuffee from Northborough, MA, USA

alt.en: Oven-baked potato fries on a tray
alt.ar: أصابع بطاطس مخبوزة في الفرن على صينية

ff_french_fries_oven.note: Golden oven-roasted fries on a baking tray, no packaging or text. Borderline: these are home-cut fries with a little black pepper, not a frozen product, but they show the oven-baked (not deep-fried) result the catalog item is about. The other candidate showed pale fries before baking (wrong state).

ff_sweet_potato_baked.reason: Only found topped/salad dishes, sweet-potato fries, USDA market-event photos, and a Japanese yakiimo street stall with people and price signs; no clean plain baked sweet potato.

ff_zucchini_boiled.reason: 4 searches (boiled zucchini, steamed zucchini, cooked courgette, zucchine lesse) returned only mixed dishes, stews and recipes; no plain boiled zucchini.

ff_eggplant_boiled.reason: Only boiled 'garden eggs' (Solanum aethiopicum - a different vegetable), salads and curries; no plain boiled aubergine.

ff_okra_boiled.reason: The one 'boiled or steamed okra' file actually shows bright, fuzzy, apparently raw pods in a pot - state not verifiable, rejected. No other plain boiled okra found.

ff_spinach_raw.reason: Candidates rejected: '1 cup of raw salad leaves' (raw baby spinach, but a measuring cup with readable '1 CUP' text), 'Fresh Spinach leaves' (WLA 2025 - actually amaranth greens held in a hand, not Spinacia), and a series of promotional 'Liat Portal for Foodie Disorder' uploads (brand in title; authorship/licence provenance doubtful).

ff_spinach_boiled.author: Laurent Nguyen

alt.en: Boiled spinach on a white plate

ff_spinach_boiled.note: Dark green wilted, boiled spinach leaves alone on a white plate; plainly cooked spinach, no seasoning or sauce visible.

ff_jute_leaves_boiled.reason: Commons has only the growing Corchorus plant, seeds, botanical plates and finished molokhia soup/stew dishes (Egyptian and Tunisian). Nothing shows plain boiled jute leaves, and the soup must not stand in for the leaves.

ff_green_beans_boiled.reason: Only raw trimmed beans, Turkish olive-oil green-bean dishes, mixed plates and a 'boiled beans' shot of dry beans; no plain boiled green beans.

ff_pepper_green_raw.author: Evan-Amos

alt.en: A whole green bell pepper

ff_pepper_green_raw.note: Single whole raw green bell pepper on a white background (Evan-Amos, public domain).

ff_pepper_red_raw.author: Evan-Amos

alt.en: A whole red bell pepper

ff_pepper_red_raw.note: Single whole raw red bell pepper on a white background (Evan-Amos, CC0).

ff_broccoli_boiled.author: FASTILY

alt.en: Cooked broccoli florets in a pan

ff_broccoli_boiled.note: Bright green cooked broccoli florets and stems in a stainless pan, no sauce or visible oil - reads as boiled/blanched broccoli. Minor clutter (pot lids) in the background.

ff_cauliflower_boiled.reason: 4 searches found only curries, rice plates, cauliflower 'rice', sauced steamed cauliflower and archival photos; no plain boiled cauliflower.

ff_beets_boiled.author: Nillerdk

alt.en: Whole boiled and peeled beetroots

ff_beets_boiled.note: Seven whole beetroots, boiled and peeled, on a plain cloth; matches boiled beetroot.

ff_taro_cooked.reason: Only near-candidate: 'Boiled taro.png' (CC BY-SA 4.0) - plain boiled taro chunks in a bowl, but it is a soft, background-removed cut-out with a clipped bowl edge. Given the rule that Egyptian vegetables must clearly look like the real thing, left missing; a human could reconsider it. Everything else was the plant, leaves, curry or historic book scans.

ff_corn_boiled.note: One husked, boiled sweet-corn cob alone on a white plate (uploader states it is regular UK sweet corn, boiled); matches the boiled ear portion.

ff_mushrooms_raw.reason: Rejected: a mature brown, soil-covered Agaricus (not the white button mushroom as sold), chopped mushrooms held in a hand, wild/unidentified white mushrooms (unsafe to show as food), and a 1024x768 file below the size floor.

ff_artichoke_boiled.author: Mauro Cateb

alt.en: Whole boiled globe artichokes on a plate

ff_artichoke_boiled.note: Four whole globe artichokes after boiling (olive-brown, softened bracts) on a white platter; matches 'artichoke, boiled, medium'. Embroidered tablecloth visible at the edges.

ff_grape_leaves_raw.author: Jon Sullivan

alt.en: Fresh green grape leaves on the vine
alt.ar: أوراق عنب خضراء طازجة على الكرمة

ff_grape_leaves_raw.note: Close-up of fresh, raw grape-vine leaves (public domain, Jon Sullivan). Borderline: the leaves are still on the vine rather than picked and stacked for cooking, but it honestly shows raw grape leaves; no harvested-leaf photo with a usable licence was found.

ff_parsley_fresh.author: Etopalrux

alt.en: A bunch of fresh flat-leaf parsley

ff_parsley_fresh.note: A full bunch of fresh flat-leaf parsley standing in a clear container of water; raw herb, no text. (Flat-leaf matches the parsley used in Egypt.)

ff_almonds.file: File:Almonds - in shell, shell cracked open, shelled, blanched.jpg
ff_almonds.author: Ivar Leidus

alt.en: Almonds in the shell, shelled and blanched

ff_almonds.note: Studio close-up (Ivar Leidus) of almonds: one in shell, one cracked open, one shelled kernel with skin and one blanched kernel. The skin-on kernel is the catalog food; the other forms are context, not a different food. Mild borderline: not a pile of kernels only, but no clean kernels-only photo was found.

ff_peanuts_roasted.reason: Both 'roasted peanuts' previews were batter/masala-coated spiced peanuts (wrong food); other hits were in-shell sand-roasted, raw peanuts (Ivar Leidus studio shot is raw, not roasted), a description naming a peanut brand, or tiny FDA recall images. No plain dry-roasted unsalted kernels found.

ff_peanut_butter.note: Macro of smooth peanut butter swirled inside an open jar; no label, brand or text visible. Matches smooth peanut butter (salt content is not visible in any photo). File is 1141x850 - above the size floor but on the small side. A sharper jar photo was rejected because a person sits in the background.

ff_walnuts.note: A walnut kernel removed intact, shown with the two shell halves it came from, on a plain surface. The kernel is the catalog food; the shell is context. Clean, no text.

ff_cashews_raw.author: Ranjithkumar Murugesan

alt.en: A pile of raw cashew nuts

ff_cashews_raw.note: Frame-filling pile of pale, unroasted whole cashew kernels; colour and matte surface match raw (not roasted) cashews. No packaging or text. (A first candidate showed the same food inside a plastic bag - rejected as packaging.)

ff_pistachios.reason: Previewed two: 'Roasted pistachio.jpg' (CC0, good roasted in-shell pistachios but laid out above a measuring ruler with printed numbers - readable text) and 'Pistachio Nuts (Unsplash).jpg' (CC0, roasted kernels in a small bowl filling only the bottom fifth of a tall frame; any square crop would show blurred city background). Other hits were GFDL-only macros, a branded 'Gold Emblem' sample, fried pistachios, or hand-held. A human could reconsider the Unsplash file with a bottom crop.

ff_mixed_nuts.author: User:Melchoir

alt.en: Roasted mixed nuts with peanuts in a glass bowl
alt.ar: مكسرات مشكلة محمصة مع فول سوداني في وعاء زجاجي

ff_mixed_nuts.note: Small glass bowl of roasted mixed nuts on white: peanuts (visible through the glass), cashews, almonds, Brazil nut, pecans and hazelnuts. Matches 'mixed nuts with peanuts, roasted'; no packaging or text.

ff_sunflower_seeds.author: Kaldari

alt.en: A shelled sunflower kernel beside a whole striped seed
alt.ar: لبّ عباد الشمس مقشّر بجانب بذرة كاملة مخططة

ff_sunflower_seeds.note: Focus-stacked studio macro on white (Kaldari, public domain): one dehulled sunflower kernel - the catalog food - next to a whole striped seed in its hull for recognition. Borderline on framing: two single seeds rather than a handful of kernels; the only other kernel candidate was actually a flower head.

ff_pumpkin_seeds.reason: The catalog item is shelled (green) kernels. The previewed 'Pumpkin seed. img 029' shows whole white in-shell seeds (the unshelled 'lib abyad' snack) - wrong state. Other hits were the in-shell roasted macro, oil-pumpkin plants, people named Pepita and archival scans; no photo of green pumpkin-seed kernels found.

ff_sesame_seeds.author: Sanjay ach

alt.en: Close-up of white sesame seeds

ff_sesame_seeds.note: Magnified white sesame seeds spread on a black background; plain dry seeds, no text. Slight note: the seeds look hulled-white while the USDA record is 'whole, dried' (which runs a little more tan) - visually the same food as sold in Egypt.

ff_chia_seeds.author: Daniel Schwen

alt.en: Close-up of dry chia seeds

ff_chia_seeds.note: Frame-filling macro of dry chia seeds (Salvia hispanica), mottled grey-brown with a few white seeds; dry as sold, not soaked. Daniel Schwen, CC BY 3.0.

ff_flaxseed.author: Sanjay Acharya

alt.en: Close-up of whole brown flaxseeds
alt.ar: صورة مقرّبة لبذور كتان بنية كاملة

ff_flaxseed.note: Frame-filling close-up of whole brown flaxseeds; dry whole seeds as sold (the catalog's default portion is whole seeds). No text or packaging.

ff_olive_oil.author: Olivenöl_Weißbrot_und_grobes_Salz.JPG: 4028mdk09 derivative work: Andrzej 22 (talk)

alt.en: Olive oil in a clear glass jug
alt.ar: زيت زيتون في إبريق زجاجي شفاف

ff_olive_oil.note: Golden-green olive oil in a plain, unlabelled glass jug on a white cloth - the plain oil itself, no olives, brand or label. A small dish of coarse salt sits in the foreground (minor extra). Crop of a larger bread-oil-salt photo. A branded jerrycan candidate was rejected; most other hits were branded bottles.

ff_sunflower_oil.reason: Previewed two: a labelled supermarket bottle (brand label, nutrition panel, barcode) and a torange.biz styled shot whose subject is a sunflower head with a corner watermark. Other hits were branded bottles, a street vendor (person), a production map and bottling-date close-ups. No plain unlabelled sunflower oil found.

ff_corn_oil.reason: The only photo titled 'Corn oil (mais)' is a branded 5-litre supermarket bottle on a shelf (rejected). 'Corn oil.jpg' is 704x1000 (below the size floor) and the rest are Mazola adverts/store shots, production maps and oil wells in corn fields. No plain unlabelled corn oil found.

ff_butter.author: Salicyna

alt.en: A block of butter on its opened wrapper

ff_butter.note: Three-quarter view of an unwrapped block of butter resting on its opened, plain foil-paper wrapper, in warm side light. Borderline on the 'packaging' rule: the wrapper is only the background, unprinted on this side, with no logo, brand or readable text. Every alternative found was a branded/wrapped pack, a dish being opened by a person, or butter on bread. Salted vs unsalted is not visible in any photo.

ff_ghee.reason: Previewed two: 'Ghee 2.jpg' (pale scraped ghee in a tub - unrecognisable, reads as ice cream) and 'Sliced clarified butter.png' (CC BY-SA 4.0, claimed own work; content is right - solid golden clarified butter in a bowl - but it is a recompressed, soft PNG at an odd 1147x867 size that looks lifted from the web, so provenance is doubtful). Other hits were ghee lamps, kettles, sweets and people/places named Ghee. A human could verify the PNG's provenance and reconsider.

ff_mayonnaise.author: Jason Terk from Somerville, MA, US

alt.en: Thick mayonnaise in a bowl with a whisk
alt.ar: مايونيز كثيف في وعاء مع مضرب يدوي

ff_mayonnaise.note: Close-up of thick, glossy mayonnaise in a bowl with a wire whisk; no jar, brand or text. Minor note: it is homemade (slightly more yellow than jarred regular mayonnaise) but visually the same food. The first candidate titled 'Mayonnaise in the bowl' was a mislabelled landscape photo.
